articles.title: Nvidia Built a CPU 'for Agents, Not Humans.' Indian Engineers Are About to Build the Apps That Run on It.
articles.excerpt: Jensen Huang's new Vera processor is going into production just as India lines up $50 billion in AI data-center spending — putting the diaspora at both ends of the agentic-AI supply chain.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, pictured in 2025.
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers write a huge share of the world's enterprise software and India is now building the data centers to run it — so Nvidia's agent-first chip lands squarely on the diaspora's turf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ISRO Hasn't Launched a Rocket Since January. A Return-to-Flight Is Now Weeks Away.
articles.excerpt: After two PSLV failures, India's space agency is targeting a late-June or early-July comeback — with the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test and a private Skyroot orbital launch waiting behind it.
articles.image_caption: An ISRO Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) on the pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who treat ISRO milestones as a source of pride and increasingly as an investable space economy, the agency's return to flight is the credibility test that unlocks both.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Arvind Krishna Just Tied IBM to ServiceNow. The Bet: Companies Want Plumbing, Not Chatbots.
articles.excerpt: IBM's long-term alliance with ServiceNow targets the messy data and legacy code that stall enterprise AI — the exact work that keeps thousands of Indian engineers and IT-services firms employed.
articles.image_caption: IBM Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna, pictured in 2025.
articles.nri_angle: The 'unglamorous' integration work IBM is betting on is precisely what employs tens of thousands of Indian engineers and props up the US revenue of TCS, Infosys and Wipro.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Just Paid $60 Billion for Cursor. The Coding Tool Half of Bengaluru Already Lives In.
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk's empire is buying the AI coding agent that automated the work of millions of engineers. For Indian developers who made Cursor a daily habit, the question is who owns their workflow now.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Cursor became the default coding tool inside Indian IT firms and Bay Area engineering teams stacked with Indian talent; an Elon Musk acquisition puts that daily workflow under new ownership just as AI is reshaping who gets hired.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Razorpay Quietly Filed for a $600 Million IPO. India's Payments War Is Headed to the Stock Market.
articles.excerpt: The Bengaluru fintech that processes payments for millions of Indian businesses wants to list by year-end — at half its 2021 peak valuation. For NRI investors, it is a direct bet on the rails the diaspora already uses to send money home.
articles.image_caption: A contactless payment made with a smartphone, the kind of digital transaction Razorpay processes for Indian merchants
articles.nri_angle: Razorpay runs the payment plumbing behind countless Indian merchants NRIs transact with daily; an IPO gives diaspora investors a rare pure-play stake in the UPI economy — but at a valuation that has been cut in half since 2021.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata's Bigbasket Just Hired an Amazon Veteran to Win the 10-Minute Grocery War
articles.excerpt: Amit Nanda, who spent more than a decade building Amazon India, takes over a Tata-backed grocery giant fighting Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart for the right to deliver in minutes.
articles.image_caption: A worker packs groceries for delivery, the operational heart of India's fast-growing quick-commerce sector
articles.nri_angle: Quick commerce reshaped how families in India shop — including the parents NRIs order groceries for from abroad; a Tata-backed leadership change signals how seriously India's biggest conglomerate is fighting for the 10-minute delivery market the diaspora increasingly relies on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wipro Just Opened a Claude Lab in Bengaluru. The Company AI Was Supposed to Gut Is Now Its Best Customer.
articles.excerpt: India's third-largest IT firm will train 10,000 engineers on Anthropic's models — a tacit admission that the only way to survive AI deflation is to sell it.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers — at Wipro's Bengaluru towers and on H-1B desks in New Jersey and the Bay Area — are watching their employers race to befriend the same AI that analysts say is eating their jobs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Chip Startups Found Money This Year. Now They Want Something Harder: Customers and the Right to Stay Indian.
articles.excerpt: Funding quadrupled in five months, but founders heading to a Nice deep-tech stage warn that without domestic buyers and IP protection, the next round will be raised — and owned — abroad.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors and returning chip engineers keep hearing that India's semiconductor story is finally real — but the founders living it say the ownership of that story is still up for grabs, and diaspora capital could decide whose flag flies over it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Startup Says It Can Make AI Video in Four Steps Instead of Fifty. It's Giving the Model Away.
articles.excerpt: Avataar.ai's Varya, backed by the India AI Mission, claims a tenfold speed jump over global rivals — and will release as an open-weight model, betting that cheap and free beats Hollywood-grade and locked.
articles.image_caption: AI video generation, the field where Avataar.ai's open Varya model aims to compete on speed and cost (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For NRI creators, founders, and small businesses, a free Indian video model that runs cheap could undercut the per-clip subscription costs of Western tools — and quietly tilt who gets to make slick content from a laptop in Edison or Wembley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Qualcomm Wants to Buy Its Way Out of the Phone. The $10 Billion Target Is Jim Keller's Chip Startup.
articles.excerpt: Qualcomm is in talks to acquire Tenstorrent for as much as $10 billion — a bet on RISC-V silicon and one of the industry's most coveted engineers, days before its make-or-break AI investor day.
articles.image_caption: Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller, the chip architect behind AMD's Zen and Apple's A-series, is the prize in Qualcomm's reported acquisition talks.
articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs thousands of Indian engineers across San Diego, Bengaluru and Hyderabad — a pivot from saturating smartphones to data-center AI silicon reshapes the career ladder and stock options for Indian chip professionals on both sides of the ocean.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Forbes Counted America's Most Successful Immigrants. 26 of the Top 250 Are Indian.
articles.excerpt: As the United States turns 250, Forbes' new ranking reads like a roll call of the diaspora — from four Big Tech CEOs to the venture capitalists quietly funding the next generation.
articles.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, one of 26 Indian-origin leaders named on Forbes' 2026 list of America's most successful immigrants.
articles.nri_angle: For every Indian American watching their kids choose between an engineering degree and a startup, the Forbes list is proof of a ceiling that no longer exists — and a map of who in the community now controls capital, code, and corporate boards.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Biggest Nvidia GPU Operator Is Going Public. For NRI Investors, It's the First Pure AI-Infrastructure Bet at Home.
articles.excerpt: Yotta Data Services is lining up a Mumbai IPO at a valuation of up to $6 billion, just as a $2.34 billion US partnership validates India's claim to be the next AI-compute hub.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia AI accelerators of the kind Yotta operates at scale across India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs have long invested back home through Indian mutual funds and real estate; Yotta's listing offers the first liquid, public way to own a slice of India's AI-compute boom — the same buildout US hyperscalers are pouring $100 billion-plus into.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Handed Siri's Brain to Sundar Pichai's Google
articles.excerpt: The new Siri in iOS 27 runs on Google's Gemini in a reported $1 billion-a-year deal. For the diaspora, the two biggest AI franchises in consumer tech now both run on Indian-led infrastructure.
articles.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, whose Gemini models will now power Apple's new Siri
articles.nri_angle: Apple's decision to power Siri with Sundar Pichai's Gemini cements Indian-origin leadership at the center of consumer AI and shifts Silicon Valley's hiring premium toward the integration and deployment roles heavily staffed by Indian and Indian-American engineers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Micron Reports June 24. The Quarter Is Priced In — the One After Isn't.
articles.excerpt: With margins near 81% and HBM sold out, Sanjay Mehrotra's memory giant is worth $1.1 trillion. NRI investors should watch the Q4 guidance, not the headline beat.
articles.image_caption: Micron Technology CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, who anchored the company's $2.75 billion chip facility in Gujarat
articles.nri_angle: Micron is a core AI holding for many NRI investors and is run by Kanpur-born Sanjay Mehrotra, who committed the first major US chip plant to India in Gujarat — making its earnings both a portfolio bellwether and a Make-in-India semiconductor milestone.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Bet Against AI Was Killing It. Now It's Partnering With the Company That Started the Panic.
articles.excerpt: Tata's IT giant will put Anthropic's Claude in the hands of 50,000 employees. It's a wager that the way past 'AI deflation' is up the value chain — and the diaspora's next jobs hang on whether it works.
articles.image_caption: Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran, who framed the TCS-Anthropic deal as equipping India's youth for the AI era
articles.nri_angle: As India's largest IT employer pivots from headcount to AI agents, the nature of US-based diaspora jobs is changing — fewer entry-level offshore-onsite roles, more demand for engineers who can architect and sell AI transformation to American enterprises.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adobe Is Tearing Down Its Paywall. Shantanu Narayen's Last Big Bet Is Free.
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO who built Adobe into a $200-billion subscription machine is now giving its AI tools away to widen the funnel — and a CFO just bolted to a chip company.
articles.image_caption: Adobe Chairman and CEO Shantanu Narayen, who is steering the company toward a freemium AI model before he steps down.
articles.nri_angle: Adobe is one of the largest employers of Indian engineers in the Bay Area and India, and its freemium gamble signals how the AI squeeze is reshaping careers and stock options for the diaspora that helped build it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UPI Just Reached the Eiffel Tower. For NRIs, the Rupee Is Quietly Going Global.
articles.excerpt: India's payment rail is now live in France, Qatar, Malaysia and a dozen other countries — turning a domestic utility into soft power, and a real convenience for the diaspora that sends money and travels home.
articles.image_caption: The Eiffel Tower in Paris, where India's UPI payment system has now gone live for tourists.
articles.nri_angle: UPI's cross-border push means NRIs can increasingly pay with an Indian app abroad and connect home remittances to a real-time rail — reshaping how the diaspora moves money between India and the West.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jayshree Ullal's Arista Built the Plumbing for the AI Boom. Now It's Going 1.6 Terabit.
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO of the most underrated company in AI just launched networking gear for racks packed with hundreds of thousands of chips — and the diaspora's quiet networking dynasty keeps compounding.
articles.image_caption: Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks, which makes the high-speed networking that ties AI data centers together.
articles.nri_angle: Jayshree Ullal is one of the wealthiest self-made women in tech and a rare Indian-origin woman running a major US chip-adjacent company; Arista's AI networking surge is a diaspora success story that rarely makes headlines next to NVIDIA.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shareholders Sue Satya Nadella's Microsoft, Saying It Hid How Much AI Was Eating Azure
articles.excerpt: A Michigan pension fund's class action accuses Microsoft of masking slowing cloud growth while quietly diverting chips to prop up Copilot. The stakes reach every Indian engineer whose stock grant is tied to MSFT.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft chairman and CEO Satya Nadella, named as a defendant in the proposed shareholder class action.
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft hold MSFT stock as a core part of their compensation, and the lawsuit's claims about Copilot's struggles cut to the heart of where their employer is betting its future.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Company's AI Agents Just Became Employees. NewCore Raised $66 Million to Give Them ID Badges.
articles.excerpt: A stealth startup from Dome9's founder argues the identity systems guarding enterprise data were built for humans logging into web apps — not millions of autonomous agents. For India's security engineers, it names the next big job market.
articles.image_caption: A data center; NewCore raised $66 million to govern the AI agents proliferating across enterprise systems (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India supplies a large share of the world's enterprise cybersecurity and identity-management engineers, and the scramble to govern AI agents is opening a new, well-funded specialization that diaspora professionals are positioned to lead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Wants to Make Its Own Memory Chips. The Minister in Charge Thinks the AI Data-Center Boom Will Force It.
articles.excerpt: Ashwini Vaishnaw says rising AI demand will pull both existing and new investors into Indian memory-chip production, as the Semiconductor Mission pivots from building fabs to designing chips and the machines that make them.
articles.image_caption: Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, who is steering India's push into memory-chip manufacturing (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For NRI semiconductor engineers and investors weighing a move home or a bet on Indian chip stocks, the shift from foreign fabs to indigenous chip design is the clearest signal yet of where the opportunities — and the jobs — will be.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satya Nadella Has a Warning for the AI Gold Rush: Don't Hand Your Company's Brain to a Stranger
articles.excerpt: Microsoft's CEO says the winners of the AI era won't be the firms with the best model, but the ones that own their own 'learning loop.' For the millions of Indians building that infrastructure, it reframes the whole job.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella, who warned that a few AI providers could capture most of the economy's value
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers build the very AI platforms Nadella warns companies not to over-rely on, and his 'human capital plus token capital' framing is a direct argument for why their judgment still matters as the tools get smarter.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Wanted Apple's Factories. Now One of Them Is Accused of Poisoning the Wells Next Door.
articles.excerpt: A Tata plant making iPhone parts near Bengaluru faces a shutdown threat over alleged groundwater contamination — a test of whether 'Make in India' can clear the bar its own farmers are setting.
articles.image_caption: Electronics quality-control inspection in India; Tata's Hosur plant assembles components for Apple's iPhone (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Every NRI cheering India's rise as Apple's factory floor now has to reckon with the cost: the Tata plant central to that story stands accused of contaminating the farmland around it, and how India handles it signals whether the manufacturing boom is built to last.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zepto Wants $10 Billion and Has 10 Months of Cash. India's First Pure Quick-Commerce IPO Is a Dare.
articles.excerpt: The Bengaluru 10-minute-delivery firm filed updated IPO papers to raise about ₹8,700 crore, with revenue up fivefold to ₹22,623 crore — and losses up nearly as fast. NRI investors get a front-row seat to a very Indian bet.
articles.image_caption: A modern fulfillment center; Zepto's 'dark store' network powers India's quick-commerce push toward a July IPO (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Zepto is the first pure-play quick-commerce company to test India's public markets, and with US backers like Contrary and Kaiser Permanente cashing out, NRI investors weighing an India allocation have to decide whether 10-minute delivery is a business or a cash bonfire.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Court Is Deciding Whether Your AI Assistant Is Allowed to Shop for You
articles.excerpt: Amazon v. Perplexity, argued before the Ninth Circuit, turns on a 1986 hacking law — and the answer will govern every AI agent built by an Indian engineer in the Valley.
articles.image_caption: Rob Sinclair via wikimedia (BY-SA)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin founders and engineers are building the agentic-AI products at the heart of this case, and the ruling will set the rules for every assistant they ship to American consumers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cognizant Slows Its India Listing Even as It Sets Aside $270 Million to Cut Jobs
articles.excerpt: The New Jersey-based IT giant says its India share sale is still 'ongoing' amid market volatility — while Project Leap reshapes a workforce that is overwhelmingly Indian.
articles.image_caption: Cognizant, which employs hundreds of thousands of staff across India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Cognizant's workforce is heavily Indian on both sides of the ocean, so its layoffs, fresher hiring reset, and India listing plans land directly on diaspora families and H-1B holders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta's First AI Data Center in India Will Be Built — and Owned — by Reliance
articles.excerpt: A 168 MW, seawater-cooled facility in Jamnagar deepens the Ambani-Zuckerberg alliance and plants Meta's AI infrastructure on Indian soil for the first time.
articles.image_caption: Meta's first India AI data center will be built and owned by Reliance (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Meta building AI capacity inside India means faster, locally-hosted services for the diaspora's families back home — and a signal to NRI investors tracking the Reliance-Meta infrastructure bet.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Qualcomm Wants Out of Your Pocket and Into the Data Center. The Bet Is on AI Inference.
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker that put Snapdragon in nearly every Android phone is now chasing a $35 billion data-center market by 2031 — and Indian engineers across its design and India teams are central to the pivot.
articles.image_caption: Qualcomm, which is pushing beyond smartphones into data-center AI inference (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm's pivot into AI data-center silicon reshapes the career map for thousands of Indian-origin chip designers in San Diego and Hyderabad — and signals where the next wave of semiconductor hiring will land.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Private Orbital Rocket Just Cleared Its Biggest Engine Test. Skyroot's Launch Window Is Open.
articles.excerpt: A successful KALAM-1200 motor test puts Hyderabad's Skyroot Aerospace — now India's first space-tech unicorn — on the final approach to a maiden Vikram-1 flight that could rewrite who launches satellites for the world.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh, India's first private rocket launch
articles.nri_angle: A private Indian company launching its own orbital rocket is a credibility marker NRIs have waited a generation for — and a live investment thesis as global funds like GIC and BlackRock pile into India's space sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Salesforce Just Paid $3.6 Billion to Buy the Robot That Answers Your Support Tickets
articles.excerpt: The acquisition of Fin — formerly Intercom — supercharges Benioff's Agentforce push and accelerates a shift that lands hardest on the Indian BPO and customer-support workforce.
articles.image_caption: Salesforce Tower in San Francisco, headquarters of the CRM giant now betting heavily on AI agents
articles.nri_angle: Salesforce's bet on autonomous customer-service agents threatens the millions of Indian jobs built on call centers and IT support — even as it expands the AI engineering roles Indian talent is racing to fill.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Just Bet $151 Million on Sarvam AI. India's IT Giants Are Done Renting Their Intelligence.
articles.excerpt: The Noida outsourcing giant is leading Sarvam's Series B and taking a 10.5% stake, a sign that India's IT services model is pivoting from selling labor to owning models.
articles.image_caption: TheStevieAwards via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: For the hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers at HCLTech, Infosys, and Wipro client sites across the US, the shift from staffing seats to owning AI models redraws what an IT-services career will look like over the next decade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adani and an Apple Supplier Are Building India's AI Data-Center Factory. The Hyperscalers Are the Customers.
articles.excerpt: Jabil, which already builds parts for Apple, is teaming with Adani to manufacture AI and data-center hardware in India, part of a planned $50 billion buildout of the country's digital backbone.
articles.image_caption: Gautam Adani, whose group is partnering with an Apple supplier to build AI data-center capacity in India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs weighing Adani-linked stocks and India's data-center boom now have a concrete signal that the country wants to manufacture AI infrastructure, not just consume it, with implications for cross-border investment and the engineers who will run it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Startup Raised $30 Million to Answer the Calls You Don't Want. NRIs With Indian Numbers Know the Pain.
articles.excerpt: Equal AI's call-screening app is built for the spam-call avalanche of Indian phone numbers, including the code-mixed Hinglish that trips up Western voice models.
articles.image_caption: The Bengaluru startup is building AI to screen the spam and scam calls that flood Indian phone numbers
articles.nri_angle: Any NRI who still keeps an Indian SIM for banking, family, or UPI knows the relentless spam-call problem; Equal AI is building voice models for exactly the multilingual, code-mixed reality the diaspora lives in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sent 44,000 Crypto Tax Notices and Found $104 Million Hidden. NRIs With Wallets Back Home Should Read the Fine Print.
articles.excerpt: A data-matching crackdown is reconciling exchange records against tax filings — and dual-status investors are squarely in its path.
articles.image_caption: Bitcoin tokens, representing cryptocurrency holdings under tax scrutiny in India
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who hold or trade crypto on Indian exchanges face a 30% flat tax, 1% TDS, and now algorithmic data-matching that flags undisclosed gains — making record-keeping a compliance necessity, not an afterthought.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Uber and Lyft Are Suing New York Over a Law That Stops Them Firing Drivers Quickly. Indian Immigrant Drivers Are Watching Closely.
articles.excerpt: Local Law 52 would bar 'wrongful deactivations' — and for the South Asian drivers who fill these fleets, a sudden app ban can mean losing a livelihood overnight.
articles.image_caption: A rideshare driver uses a smartphone navigation app inside a car at night
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of South Asian immigrants drive for Uber and Lyft in U.S. cities; a law limiting arbitrary 'deactivations' directly affects their job security, while the platforms argue it forces them to keep unsafe drivers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Funding Its Own Eyes in the Sky. A Bengaluru Startup Just Won a Grant to Build AI That Sees the Subcontinent.
articles.excerpt: SatSure's $2.6 million award is a small cheque with a big idea behind it: sovereign Earth-observation models trained on India's own land, not borrowed from the West.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: India's push for sovereign space-AI infrastructure opens cross-border investment and engineering opportunities for NRIs in deep tech, while reducing the country's dependence on foreign satellite-data providers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tech Back Office Is Now the Brain. Its Workforce Is About to Cross 2.36 Million.
articles.excerpt: A US cybersecurity firm just opened a Bengaluru capability center and pledged to grow it 50% in six months. The reason was not cost — it was talent the company could not find anywhere else.
articles.image_caption: A technology park in Bengaluru, the hub of India's global capability center boom
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing a return to India, the global capability center boom now offers headquarters-grade work — product, R&D, and AI engineering — at home rather than a back-office demotion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bay Area Tech Layoffs Hit 9,284 — Already Worse Than All of Last Year. For H-1B Workers, the Clock Starts Ticking.
articles.excerpt: Fresh WARN filings push 2026's regional job cuts past the entire first half of 2025, with six months still to run. For visa holders, a layoff opens a 60-day countdown that most American colleagues never have to think about.
articles.image_caption: Office workstations in a Silicon Valley technology company
articles.nri_angle: A pink slip means a 60-day grace period to find a new sponsor or leave the country — a deadline that turns every layoff round into an immigration emergency for thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B and L-1 visas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: $1.3 Trillion Vanished From AI Chip Stocks in a Week. Then They Had Their Best Day in a Year.
articles.excerpt: A single cautious sentence from Broadcom triggered one of the sharpest semiconductor selloffs in years — and a violent rebound days later. For Indian-American investors and tech workers paid in stock, the whiplash is the new normal.
articles.image_caption: A close-up of a semiconductor wafer used in advanced AI chips
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American households are heavily concentrated in tech equities and equity compensation — RSUs, ESPPs, and chip-heavy index funds — so a $1.3 trillion swing in AI semiconductors lands directly on diaspora net worth, not just on Wall Street screens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sriram Krishnan Wrote America's AI Playbook. Now He's Leaving the White House to Build His Own.
articles.excerpt: The Chennai-born policy adviser shaped the AI Action Plan, brokered government access to frontier models, and navigated the Anthropic crisis. His next move is a startup.
articles.image_caption: Sriram Krishnan, former White House senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence
articles.nri_angle: The most senior Indian-American in US AI policy is leaving at a moment when AI export controls directly threaten Indian IT firms and the 300,000 Indian-origin professionals in American tech.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Launching 16 Electric Vehicles in Nine Months. For Every New Petrol Car, Two EVs Are Pulling Up.
articles.excerpt: Starting this week, Mercedes, Tata, Toyota, BYD, Mahindra, and Maruti are flooding India's market with EVs and plug-in hybrids. The ratio to new ICE models is 2:1.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Tata Motors and Mahindra stand to benefit from India's EV leadership, while the charging infrastructure buildout changes the experience of visiting India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Razorpay Just Filed for a $600 Million IPO. India's Payments War Is About to Go Public.
articles.excerpt: The fintech giant's confidential filing targets a $5–6 billion valuation — well below its 2021 peak — as Indian startups rush to prove they can survive the public markets.
articles.image_caption: The Razorpay logo — the Bengaluru-based payment gateway has filed for a $600 million IPO (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Razorpay processes $180 billion in annual payments including cross-border UPI transactions — making it the invisible plumbing behind every NRI's Swiggy order, Zerodha trade, or Zomato delivery. Its IPO is a litmus test for whether India's fintech boom can deliver public-market returns to diaspora investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zoho Built Its Own Server in Nagpur. It Took Five Years and a Mountain Pass's Name.
articles.excerpt: The 'Nathu La' platform — designed entirely in India on Intel Xeon 6 chips — cuts power consumption by 18% and ownership costs by 30%, marking Zoho's entry into the sovereign hardware race.
articles.image_caption: Sridhar Vembu, founder and CEO of Zoho Corporation, which built its Nathu La server platform in Nagpur (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Zoho serves 100 million users worldwide, including tens of thousands of Indian-origin small business owners in the US. Its move into India-designed hardware signals that Indian tech sovereignty is no longer just a government talking point — it's being built by private companies, with IP owned entirely in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'AI Deflation' Is Squeezing India's IT Giants. Their Own Employees See It First.
articles.excerpt: HCLTech warns of a 3-5% revenue hit. TCS has shed 23,000 workers. Infosys is down 35% from its peak. The $315 billion Indian IT sector is learning what it means to be disrupted by the technology it sells.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru — India's IT services giants face margin pressure as AI automates traditional outsourcing work (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of NRIs work at or have family in India's big IT firms — and the stocks are staples in Indian household portfolios. AI deflation threatens both careers and savings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American Cybersecurity Giants Are Racing to Arm India's 75 Million Small Businesses
articles.excerpt: As AI-powered attacks surge post-Claude Mythos, Palo Alto Networks and Microsoft are pitching cut-rate security to Indian MSMEs — a market that accounts for nearly a third of India's GDP.
articles.image_caption: Palo Alto Networks headquarters — American cybersecurity firms are expanding rapidly into India's small business market (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs invest in or run family businesses in India. The $3.4 billion cybersecurity surge affects both their portfolio picks (PANW, MSFT) and the family firms back home increasingly under AI-driven attack.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satya Nadella Wants to Kill the App. Project Solara Is How.
articles.excerpt: Microsoft's Build 2026 flagship isn't a new Office feature or a Copilot upgrade. It's an entire operating system — built on Android, not Windows — where AI agents replace apps entirely.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event
articles.nri_angle: Satya Nadella continues to define the AI-first era from the CEO chair. For the tens of thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft and its partner ecosystem, Solara signals a fundamental shift in what they'll be building.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asha Sharma's 100-Day Verdict on Xbox: 'This Cannot Continue'
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO's reset memo reveals a gaming division bleeding money at 3% margins, a hardware crisis that has quintupled component costs, and a parent company that hasn't ruled out selling the whole thing.
articles.image_caption: Asha Sharma, who became Xbox president and COO in March 2025 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin executive now holds the reins of one of gaming's most consequential turnarounds — and her decisions will ripple through thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft's global workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sundar Pichai Is Selling $85 Billion of Alphabet to Win the AI Race. Investors Are Divided.
articles.excerpt: The largest equity offering in tech history includes a $10 billion anchor from Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway. Alphabet plans to spend up to $190 billion this year alone — and it ordered three million TPUs from Intel.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google
articles.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's most consequential financial gamble reshapes the company tens of thousands of Indian engineers call home — and it may determine whether Google or OpenAI defines the next era of computing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Just Put 120 Indian Deep-Tech Startups on a Stage in Nice. The Money Is Listening.
articles.excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026 brings Indian semiconductor, space, and biotech ventures face-to-face with 500 global investors — and it's happening the day before the G7.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who co-inaugurated Bharat Innovates 2026 with French President Macron in Nice
articles.nri_angle: For NRI founders, investors, and professionals debating whether India's deep-tech ecosystem is real, Bharat Innovates is the strongest signal yet that New Delhi is channelling state machinery into turning lab breakthroughs into global businesses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel's Stock Has Surged 450% This Year. Lip-Bu Tan's Foundry Gamble Is Starting to Pay Off.
articles.excerpt: Bank of America just double-upgraded Intel to Buy after foundry wins from Google, Microsoft, and potentially Nvidia. The chip giant's most troubled division is becoming its strongest story.
articles.image_caption: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has overseen the company's foundry revival since taking the helm in 2025
articles.nri_angle: Intel's revival directly affects the tens of thousands of Indian engineers who work at the company and across its supply chain — and its American foundry buildout could reshape the H-1B landscape for semiconductor talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
